answer.headline: Highest tight-capacity passenger shares in CY2025, with taxi-out and busiest hour where On-Time exists

claims.text: In CY2025 ({F370.period}), calculated tight-capacity passenger share is {F370} at STC, {F314} at PVU, {F322} at RFD, {F119} at EAT, {F228} at LNK, {F358} at SJU, {F127} at ERI, {F59} at BQN, {F220} at LCK, and {F32} at AZA.
AZA {F422} outranks SGF {F423}, and share {F32} is not equal to share {F350}, so the cutoff is not a tie.
Flight-weighted average taxi-out for the ranked airports with On-Time taxi-out observations, excluding EAT, is {F796} ({F796.class}) in {F796.period}.

STC taxi-out is {F786} and busiest scheduled hour is {F795}.
PVU taxi-out is {F783} and busiest scheduled hour is {F792}.
RFD taxi-out is {F784} and busiest scheduled hour is {F793}.
LNK taxi-out is {F782} and busiest scheduled hour is {F791}.
SJU taxi-out is {F785} and busiest scheduled hour is {F794}.
ERI taxi-out is {F780} and busiest scheduled hour is {F789}.
BQN taxi-out is {F779} and busiest scheduled hour is {F788}.
LCK taxi-out is {F781} and busiest scheduled hour is {F790}.
AZA taxi-out is {F778} and busiest scheduled hour is {F787}.
Because busiest scheduled hour is defined airport by airport, the airport-level figures are the aggregate of peak hour scheduled operations. A set total is not a meaningful reading of that metric.

A high tight-capacity passenger share may come from scheduling on a thin set of routes. That cause is not established, and the share does not measure unmet demand, terminal capacity, or profitability.

assumptions: The rank covers US airports whose latest calendar-year enplanements meet the commercial floor used for this entity set. Airports under that floor are outside the order.
Tight-capacity passenger share uses the catalog default threshold in {F370.definition}. A stricter threshold was not applied.
Higher share ranks higher. The rank tool also stores a set-relative min-max score. That score is not a valuation and would change if the airport set changed.

Peak hour scheduled operations is read as busiest scheduled hour: the maximum, over date and local hour, of scheduled arrivals plus departures on reporting-carrier operated flights. The percentile form of scheduled peak is not used.
Taxi-out and busiest hour are limited to On-Time months inside CY2025 ({F796.period}), because a full CY2025 window is out of coverage for On-Time.
The pooled taxi-out leaves out EAT, which has no On-Time rows in that window.
limitations: Full CY2025 average taxi-out and busiest scheduled hour are not established. On-Time data do not cover the early months of CY2025.
EAT has no On-Time observations in the covered months, so taxi-out and busiest hour are missing for EAT.

ERI, PVU, and SJU, plus the group taxi-out total, sit below the On-Time coverage threshold. Those figures describe reporting-carrier domestic flights, and a partial slice where the low-coverage flag applies.
Busiest scheduled hour is a lower bound from reporting carriers and cannot be added across airports.
The group taxi-out is flight-weighted. It will not match an equal-weight mean of the airport-level taxi-out figures.
Tight-capacity passenger share does not measure unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, or profitability.
Some airports above the enplanement floor had no computed share and were not scored. They are absent from this order.
This is not the investment screening model, so screening flags and the screen tie band do not apply. Here a tie would mean equal shares, and the cutoff shares are not equal.
